applicant_utility.summary: The Helmut Veith Stipend gives female computer science master's students EUR 7,000 per year plus a full tuition fee waiver at TU Wien, and it is open to applicants to any of eight English-taught CS master's programmes including Logic and Artificial Intelligence, Software Engineering, Visual Computing and Embedded Computing Systems. The annual deadline is 30 November, and you may apply for the stipend before or in parallel with your admission. The catch is that funding is only released once you have unconditional admission, so the stipend application and the admissions application have to be run in parallel, not one after the other.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Women with a strong mathematics and technical foundation in one of Helmut Veith's fields - logic in computer science, computer-aided verification, software engineering or computer security - who want an English-taught TU Wien master's in an area where they already have depth. Applicants who intend to build that background during their studies are explicitly welcome too, so a demonstrable aptitude and a plan count alongside completed coursework.
application_readiness_checklist: Pick one of the eight English-taught Master's Programmes in Computer Science at TU Wien and confirm you are eligible for admission
Start the admission application in parallel - the stipend does not replace it
Note your mathematical and technical background against logic, verification, software engineering or computer security
Prepare the electronic application in the TU Wien job portal
Submit the stipend application before 30 November
Hold any evidence you will need for the admission decision (transcripts, degree certificate, English proof)
common_rejection_risks: Assuming the stipend application covers the admissions application - TU Wien states it does not
Applying while holding only a conditional admission or no admission yet and expecting payment
Choosing a Computer Science-related master's programme that is not on the eight-programme English-taught list
No evidence of mathematical or technical depth in any of Helmut Veith's fields
Expecting the stipend to cover rent and living costs - it does not
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Even with the tuition waiver, you must fund approximately EUR 11,000 to 15,000 a year of living costs in Vienna, plus the Students Union fee, health insurance, travel and any material costs, out of the EUR 7,000 and your own funds.
applicant_utility.document_audit: TU Wien does not publish a document list for this stipend beyond the job-portal application, so keep your degree certificate, transcripts, English-language proof and CV ready for immediate upload when the portal form requests them.

applicant_utility.summary: Mannagetta Fellowships are completion fellowships of EUR 25,000 for twelve months, aimed at doctoral candidates in Austria in archaeology, ancient and medieval history, art and music history, philosophy or law who started their doctorate no more than three years ago and need exactly one more year to finish. There are only one or two fellowships per year, so the pool is very small. The strongest part of the file is the supervisor's statement, which has to confirm that third-party or institute funding is not possible - that is the gate that makes this a completion fellowship rather than a general stipend.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Late-stage doctoral candidates in the seven eligible disciplines who have a complete, realistic twelve-month writing plan and whose supervisor will state that no other funding route exists. Anyone whose doctorate started more than three years ago, or who needs more than twelve months, should look elsewhere - the rules on both are explicit and unforgiving.
application_readiness_checklist: Confirm your doctoral or PhD studies at an Austrian university started no more than three years before the submission date
Confirm your dissertation is in archaeology, prehistory and early history, ancient history and medieval history, art history and music history, philosophy, or law
Draft the 10 to 15 page project description: theoretical foundations, research questions, preparatory work, detailed time and work plan
Write the German abstract of the project description (1 to 2 pages)
Assemble the list of all examinations passed during doctoral studies and the Master's certificate
Ask your supervisor for the written statement, including the confirmation that third-party or institute financing is not possible
Prepare the CV and publication list
Merge into two unprotected PDF files of at most 10 MB each and register in the OeAW online form
Return the signed printed form by replying to the confirmation e-mail
common_rejection_risks: Missing the hard 2 p.m. CEST cut-off on 20 October 2026 - after receipt, changes or additional documents are not possible
Doctoral studies that started more than three years before submission
A project description shorter than 10 pages or longer than 15, or without a detailed time and work plan
A supervisor statement that omits the confirmation that third-party or institute funding is not possible
Protected or password-secured PDFs, or a single file over 10 MB
A dissertation outside the seven listed subject areas
A work plan that plainly needs more than twelve months
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The OeAW publishes no statement on what the EUR 25,000 covers or what it excludes. Any travel, translation, publication or additional academic costs during the twelve months need to be met from the stipend itself or from other funds.
applicant_utility.document_audit: Two PDFs maximum, unprotected, 10 MB each. Keep the German abstract inside the correct file so the reviewer does not have to hunt for it. Check the printing of the signed form and send the reply e-mail from the same account that registered the application.
